topic_concept: Image Formation and Aperture of Convex Lens
question_text: A student forms a sharp image of a lighted candle on a screen using a convex lens of focal length 15 cm. The lower half of the lens is now covered with black paper. What happens to the image on the screen?
correct_answer_and_steps: The image remains completely intact and full. Every exposed portion of the lens refracts light rays from all parts of the object. Covering half the lens reduces the light energy transmitted, decreasing brightness without cropping.
student_response: The top half of the candle image is completely missing because the bottom half of the lens is covered.
evidence_rationale: Believes covering half the lens cuts the image in half, misunderstanding that every point on the lens receives light from every point on the object.
diagram_description: Convex lens with lower half covered by black opaque cardboard. Object placed beyond 2F forms a complete real inverted image on the screen with reduced brightness.

question_text: A person with a far point of 150 cm cannot see distant stars clearly. What eye defect do they have and which lens will restore clear vision?
correct_answer_and_steps: The defect is Myopia (nearsightedness), where parallel rays from distant objects converge in front of the retina. A Concave (diverging) lens is required.
student_response: Condition is Myopia. It is corrected by using spectacles with concave lenses of appropriate focal length.
evidence_rationale: Rigorous scientific reasoning with valid physical principles and mathematical steps.
diagram_description: Myopic eye where rays from distant object focus in front of the retina. Concave diverging lens corrects focus back onto the retina.

topic_concept: Dispersion of White Light through a Glass Prism
question_text: When a narrow beam of white light passes through a glass prism, it splits into a band of seven colours. Which colour bends the most, and which colour travels fastest inside the glass?
correct_answer_and_steps: Violet bends the most because it has the shortest wavelength and experiences the highest refractive index in glass. Red travels fastest in glass and deviates the least.
student_response: Red bends the most because red is the strongest colour and has the most energy.
misconception_label: MISC-EYE-002: Prism Dispersion Speed and Deviation Inversion
evidence_rationale: Believes red bends the most because it is 'strongest', or claims violet travels fastest inside the glass medium.
diagram_description: White light beam incident on triangular glass prism dispersing into VIBGYOR spectrum. Red refracts least, Violet refracts most.

evidence_rationale: Applies W = F × d without considering the angle between force and displacement; believes work is done whenever force is applied even if perpendicular to motion.
diagram_description: Block being pushed horizontally while normal force acts vertically — illustrating perpendicular force does zero work.

question_text: A 2 kg ball moving at 2 m/s collides with an identical stationary ball. Ball 1 stops. What is velocity of ball 2?

misconception_label: MISC-MOM-001: Momentum Not Conserved When Object Stops
evidence_rationale: Believes momentum is destroyed or disappears when one object stops, rather than being transferred to another object; violates conservation of momentum.
